hook.line: After a day when everything went wrong at the café, somebody has to take the blame, and somebody deserves the credit. Spanish has a short phrase for each.

examples.en: It was your fault. (to a friend)

examples.es: Llegamos tarde por culpa del tráfico.
examples.en: We were late because of the traffic.

examples.es: Gracias a ella, todo salió bien.
examples.en: Thanks to her, everything went well.

examples.es: Gracias a Hernando, llegamos a tiempo.
examples.en: Thanks to Hernando, we arrived on time.

rule:
For blame, *Fue culpa* plus who: *mía*, *tuya*, *suya*, *nuestra*, or *de* plus a name (*de Simón*). The little word comes after *culpa*, and *fue mi culpa* works too.
For a bad result with a cause, *por culpa de*: *por culpa del tráfico* (*de* plus *el* makes *del*).
For credit, *gracias a*: *gracias a ella*.
So "because of" has two Spanish faces. Bad news gets *por culpa de*, good news gets *gracias a*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *mía*, *tuya* and *nuestra* the long possessives: they come after the noun and stand firmly on their own.

readAndPick.es: Llegamos tarde por culpa del tráfico.
options: We were late thanks to the traffic.
We were late because of the traffic.

readAndPick.es: Gracias a ella, todo salió bien.
options: Because of her, everything went wrong.
Thanks to her, everything went well.

readAndPick.es: Gracias a Vale, el café sigue abierto.
options: The café is still open, and Vale is to blame.
The café is still open thanks to Vale.

readAndPick.es: Se cayó por culpa de la lluvia.
options: He fell because of the rain.
He fell thanks to the rain.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Fue culpa ___.* (*mía* or *mío*) It was my fault.
yourTurn.why: *Culpa* is feminine, so the long word is *mía*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Llegamos tarde ___ tráfico.* (*por culpa del* or *gracias al*) We were late because of the traffic.
yourTurn.answer: Llegamos tarde por culpa del tráfico.
yourTurn.why: Being late is bad news, so blame: *por culpa del*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ Hernando, llegamos a tiempo.* (*Por culpa de* or *Gracias a*) Thanks to Hernando, we arrived on time.
yourTurn.answer: Gracias a Hernando, llegamos a tiempo.
yourTurn.why: Arriving on time is good news, so credit: *gracias a*.

yourTurn.prompt: To a friend: It was your fault.

yourTurn.why: Blame for a person is *culpa de* plus the name.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about us: *Fue culpa mía.*
Say: We missed the bus because of me.
yourTurn.answer: Perdimos el bus por culpa mía.
accept: Perdimos el bus por mi culpa.
yourTurn.why: Missing the bus is bad, so *por culpa*, and for yourself *mía*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. For yourself, Spanish uses *mía*, not *de mí*.
Close. For your friend it is *tuya*, a single word.

pitfalls.wrong: Por culpa de ella, todo salió bien.
pitfalls.right: Gracias a ella, todo salió bien.
pitfalls.why: *Por culpa de* blames. When things go well, thank with *gracias a*.

personal: Think of the last time something went wrong, or right, this week. Write one sentence with *fue culpa de…* or *por culpa de…*, and one with *gracias a…* for someone who helped.
